synonyms: ["Arthritis Associated With Psoriasis", "Arthritis With Psoriasis", "Joint Inflammation In Psoriasis Patients", "Psoriasis-related Arthritis", "Psoriasis-related Joint Inflammation"]
conventional_description: Psoriatic arthritis is a chronic autoimmune condition that causes inflammation in the joints and often occurs alongside the skin disease psoriasis. It can affect any joint, leading to pain, swelling, stiffness, and in some cases permanent joint damage. Diagnosis is based on a combination of skin and nail changes, joint symptoms, and sometimes imaging or blood tests to rule out other forms of arthritis. The severity varies widely - some people have mild, occasional flares, while others experience progressive joint destruction.
conventional_treatments: Conventional treatment typically starts with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain and inflammation. For persistent disease, disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) like methotrexate are used to slow joint damage. Biologic medications that target specific parts of the immune system (TNF inhibitors, IL-17 inhibitors, etc.) have transformed care for many patients. Corticosteroid injections or short courses may be used for severe flares, and physical therapy helps maintain mobility.
tcm_understanding:
TCM views psoriatic arthritis as a combination of two problems: a skin condition (白疕, bái bǐ) and a painful obstruction syndrome (痹, bì) in the joints. The skin plaques reflect heat, dryness, or stagnation in the blood, while the joint pain stems from external pathogenic factors - Wind, Cold, Damp, or Heat - that have invaded the body and lodged in the channels. When the protective Qi is weak, these evils can penetrate the joints and block the flow of Qi and Blood, causing pain and swelling.
In the Wind-Cold-Damp pattern, Cold tightens the channels and Damp creates heaviness and swelling. The joints feel worse in cold, damp weather and better with warmth. The skin plaques tend to be pale red with thick, white scales, and the tongue is pale with a white coating.
In the Damp Heat pattern, Heat and Damp combine to create hot, red, swollen joints that feel better with cold. The skin patches are brighter red, and the tongue becomes red with a thick, yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is rapid and slippery.
A third, less common pattern - Heat invading the channels - causes an acute, fiery inflammation. Joints suddenly become red, hot, and intensely painful, often with fever and thirst. This pattern requires prompt treatment to clear the heat and cool the blood.
Because psoriatic arthritis can shift over time - a cold, stiff joint in winter might become hot and swollen during a flare - TCM treatment is tailored to the current presentation. A practitioner will examine your tongue, feel your pulse, and ask detailed questions about what makes your joints better or worse to identify which pattern is dominant.
classical_quote: 「白疕，其状白色，搔之则白屑出，痒如虫行。」
classical_translation: "Bai Bi (white crust) appears as white patches; when scratched, white scales fall off, and itching is like insects crawling."

tcm_diagnosis:
A TCM practitioner starts by asking how your joints feel and what your skin plaques look like, because psoriatic arthritis (白疕痹) always combines skin and joint signs. The quality of joint pain, the color of the plaques, and what makes symptoms better or worse are the first clues that point toward one pattern rather than another.
If the pain feels deep, heavy, and stiff, and cold or damp weather makes it much worse, the Wind-Cold-Damp pattern is likely. The skin patches tend to be pale red with thick white scales, and the tongue may look pale with a thin white coating. A wiry or slow pulse often confirms this cold, stuck picture.
When joints are red, hot, and swollen, especially during a flare, a practitioner thinks of Damp Heat in the channels. The skin plaques are brighter red, and the tongue coating turns thick, yellow, and greasy. A rapid, slippery pulse matches this inflammatory, damp-heat presentation and sets it apart from the cold pattern.
A less common but more acute picture is Heat invading the channels. Here joint pain is severe, with intense redness and swelling, and the person may feel feverish. The tongue is deep red with a yellow coating, and the pulse is rapid and forceful. This pattern demands urgent attention because the heat is overwhelming the body’s cooling systems.

patterns.symptoms: ["Joint pain and stiffness that worsens in cold or damp weather", "Swelling around joints without redness or heat", "Heaviness, numbness or tingling in the limbs", "Skin plaques are pale or light red with thick, dry white scales", "Aversion to cold or wind, with cold hands and feet", "Pain may shift from joint to joint or stay in one place"]
patterns.worse_with: Cold, damp, or windy weather, Prolonged rest or inactivity, Raw, cold foods and icy drinks
patterns.better_with: Warmth (heating pad, warm bath), Gentle, regular movement, Dry, sunny weather, Warm, cooked meals with spices
patterns.why_this_happens: Wind, Cold and Damp are external evils that invade the body when the protective Qi is weak. They lodge in the channels, joints and skin. Cold constricts and freezes - it tightens the channels and makes the pain worse in cold weather. Damp is heavy and sticky - it causes swelling, a sensation of weight, and makes the joints feel stiff and sluggish. Wind makes the pain move around. When these three evils block the flow of Qi and Blood, the joints become painful and stiff, and the skin loses its nourishment, producing the pale, thick-scaled plaques of psoriasis. Over time, the obstruction can become fixed and cause chronic joint damage.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, slightly swollen body with teeth marks, white greasy coating. Pulse: wiry (xian) and tight (jin), or soggy (ru) and slow.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and Damp are the very evils that cause this pattern - they constrict the channels and weigh down the limbs. Warmth and movement push Qi and Blood through the blockages, like a stream melting ice. Dry weather and warming foods reduce the environmental Dampness and internal Cold, giving the joints and skin a chance to heal.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the body warm and dry - a hot water bottle or warm bath can soothe stiff joints. Gentle daily movement like walking or tai chi keeps Qi and Blood flowing without overstraining. Favour warm, cooked foods such as soups, stews, ginger, cinnamon and black pepper. Avoid raw, cold foods, icy drinks and dairy, which can increase internal Dampness. Protect yourself from wind and rain, and consider wearing natural fibres that breathe.

patterns.why_this_happens: When the body is invaded by Dampness and Heat, these two pathogens combine into a sticky, inflammatory obstruction that settles in the joints and channels. The Dampness makes the joints feel heavy, swollen, and stiff, while the Heat brings redness, warmth, and sharp pain. In psoriatic arthritis, this pattern often appears during acute flares, where the same Damp-Heat that can fuel skin plaques now congests the joints, severely limiting movement.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: Red body, possibly slightly swollen, with a yellow greasy coating. Pulse: Slippery and rapid, may feel soggy or have a wiry quality at the middle position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Damp-Heat is a combination of two pathogenic factors that create inflammation and obstruction. Heat aggravates the Heat component, so cold compresses and cool environments soothe the joints. Dampness is sticky and heavy; greasy foods and humid weather add more Dampness, worsening swelling and stiffness. Light, cooling foods help clear Heat and drain Dampness, while gentle movement prevents stagnation without overheating.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid greasy, spicy, and deep-fried foods that generate Damp-Heat. Favor cooling, light foods like cucumber, mung bean, and barley. Keep your living space dry and cool, and consider gentle water-based exercise to move the joints without overheating.

patterns.why_this_happens: External heat pathogens, such as wind-heat or summer-heat, can directly invade the body and lodge in the channels and joints. This sudden assault creates intense Heat and stagnation, blocking the flow of Qi and Blood. The result is an acute, fiery inflammation: joints become red, swollen, and painfully hot to the touch.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with yellow coating (greasy or dry), possibly with red prickles. Pulse: rapid (shu) and slippery (hua), may feel overflowing (hong), forceful especially at the Guan positions.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Heat invading the channels is a classic Full-Heat pattern, so anything that adds more Heat-like spicy food, alcohol, or warm environments-will intensify the redness, swelling, and pain. Cold applications and cooling foods directly counteract the pathogenic Heat, calming the inflammation and soothing the joints. Rest prevents further Qi stagnation and allows the body to direct its energy toward clearing the invasion.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: During an acute flare, rest the affected joints and apply cool (not ice-cold) compresses for relief. Eat plenty of cooling foods like cucumber, watermelon, and mung beans, while strictly avoiding alcohol, spicy dishes, and fried or greasy foods that add internal Heat.

formulas.translation: Four Marvel Powder · Qīng dynasty, 1904 CE
formulas.properties: Cool, Clears Heat and dries Dampness, Clears Damp-Heat from the Lower Burner, Strengthens the Spleen and Resolves Dampness
formulas.description: A classical four-herb formula used to clear heat and dampness from the lower body. It is commonly applied for hot, swollen, painful joints (especially in the knees and feet), lower limb weakness, and conditions like gout and eczema that involve a combination of inflammation and heavy, waterlogged tissue. The formula works by cooling inflammation, drying excess moisture, strengthening digestion to stop dampness at its source, and directing the formula's effects downward to the legs and lower body.

formulas.description: A classical formula for joint inflammation with strong internal Heat. It combines powerful fever-reducing and fluid-replenishing herbs with Cinnamon Twig (Gui Zhi) to open the channels and relieve joint pain. Originally used for a type of malaria with predominantly hot symptoms and aching bones, it is now widely applied for conditions like acute gout, rheumatic fever, and inflammatory arthritis when joints are red, hot, swollen, and painful alongside fever, thirst, and sweating.

faqs.question: Can TCM treat both the skin and joint symptoms of psoriatic arthritis?
faqs.answer: Yes. TCM sees the skin and joints as connected through the same underlying pattern. For example, if Damp Heat is the root, both the red, scaly plaques and the hot, swollen joints are treated with herbs that clear heat and dry dampness. Acupuncture points are chosen to address both the channels and the blood, so treatment is integrated, not separate.

faqs.question: How long until I see improvement?
faqs.answer: Many patients notice less joint stiffness and pain after 3-4 weeks of consistent treatment. The skin may take a bit longer - often 6-8 weeks to see visible changes in plaques. Acute flares usually respond more quickly. Remember, TCM aims to correct the underlying imbalance, so full benefit often builds over several months.

faqs.question: Can I continue my biologic medications while doing TCM?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes. Herbal formulas and acupuncture can complement conventional treatment. However, some herbs may interact with immunosuppressants, so it’s essential to inform both your rheumatologist and your TCM practitioner about all medications and supplements you’re taking. Never stop or adjust your prescribed medications without your doctor’s guidance.

faqs.question: What foods should I avoid?
faqs.answer: Generally, it’s wise to avoid foods that create dampness and heat - such as greasy, fried foods, excessive alcohol, sugar, and dairy. If you have a cold-damp pattern, raw and cold foods can worsen stiffness. Your TCM practitioner will give you specific dietary advice based on your pattern, but starting with a warm, cooked, whole-foods diet is a good baseline.

faqs.question: Does acupuncture hurt?
faqs.answer: Acupuncture needles are extremely thin - much finer than injection needles. Most people feel a brief prick or a dull ache when the needle is inserted, but it’s rarely painful. Many patients actually find the sessions deeply relaxing. The points used for psoriatic arthritis are typically on the limbs and back, and the treatment is tailored to your comfort.

faqs.question: Is psoriatic arthritis curable with TCM?
faqs.answer: TCM cannot cure the autoimmune tendency, but it can significantly reduce the frequency and severity of flares, relieve pain, and improve quality of life. Many patients achieve long periods of remission where joints are pain-free and skin is clear. The goal is to bring the body back into balance so that symptoms become minimal and manageable.

research.title: Evidence-based clinical practice guideline for psoriasis vulgaris (Bai Bi) in Chinese medicine
research.description: This 2013 guideline, developed by the China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, provides standardized pattern differentiation (including Wind-Cold-Damp, Damp Heat, and Blood Heat patterns) and recommended formulas and acupuncture points for psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. It serves as a foundational reference for TCM management.
